newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares fall sharply, pulled down by OTE.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares fall sharply, pulled down by OTE.

text.p: Greek shares shed 2.94 percent on Tuesday on low to moderate turnover and brokers attributed the sharp fall to the disappointing performance of OTE shares that adversely affected market sentiment depressing prices across-the-board.
Monday was a market holiday in Greece and the bourse was closed.

"All eyes were on OTE today and many investors, watching the sharp fall in OTE shares, opted to liquidate positions in other blue-chips driving the general index lower," said Nick Kapatos, broker at Nexus Securities.
Kapatos echoed other brokers and analysts who claimed that market makers in OTE shares wanted the stock to consolidate for a while and rise smoothly afterwards in reaction to good corporate news.
"Sentiment was adversely affected by the behaviour of OTE today but macroeconomic fundamentals remain strong and OTE has proven a good, long-term investment rather than a short-term play," he said.
Some analysts said they expected the market to rebound upon the release of surplus liquidity from OTE's private placement and public offering.
The large part-float of OTE telecom was completed on Friday.
OTE's second part-flotation was oversubscribed three times, forcing global coordinators to size down the allocation to some 245,000 retail investors to 80 shares.
The price that emerged from the book-building process for institutional investors was 6,600 drachmas per share, while that for retail investors was 6,400 drachmas.
The Greek State lowered its stake in OTE's share capital from 92.43 percent to around 80.0, offering a total of 53.4 million shares.
Starting on June 18, OTE will tap the market with a 7.5 percent, 190 billion drachma rights issue of 31.6 million shares at 6,000 drachmas each.
The Athens general index drifted 2.94 percent or 47.78 points to close at 1,577.95 from Friday's 1,625.73 close.
Turnover reached 18.88 billion drachmas on volume of 3.84 million shares.
